correctness.rationale: For all k>=3 and standard Euclidean roots, the proof uses the exact barycentric minimum-ball identity. At k=3, weights (7,9,1,1,9,7)/34 are positive and all six Gram products equal 6/17. For k>=4 the symmetric two-arm coefficients w_j=alpha/2*(L+1-j)*(a-L-1+j) are strictly positive, sum 1/2 on each branch, and yield support Gram products alpha=3(2L+1)/(L(L+1)(L^2+L+1)). Both excluded arcs have Gram product w_L>alpha, where w_L-alpha=3(L^2-2L-1)/(L(L+1)(L^2+L+1))>0 for L>=3. All roots have squared norm 2. The certificate proves unique global center, exact radius, all contact classes, and strict clearance; rational recomputation from the delivered code verifies k=3..70. These finite checks are corroborative, not an infinite proof. Direct closed expressions include no unproved exceptional ranges.

value.rationale: Minimal adjacent interchange of opposite signs at the interface of the k/k block orientation is the nearest nontrivial perturbation of a well-defined extremal balanced cycle root-polytope. The family preserves all oriented-cycle face data, yet its intrinsic Euclidean minimum sphere changes and undergoes a sharp exceptional transition at k=3 versus all k>=4. A true two-arc screening calculation gives the full optimal center, all 2k contact decisions, exact positive clearance, and quantitative squared-radius defect 9k/((k-1)(k^2+2)(k^2-k+1)); the dimension-dependent contact phenomenon is not a textbook normalization or known-table recomputation. The result resolves the true optimum specifically where canonical rank-sphere feasibility fails, supplying an explicit active-set stability boundary useful for studying nearby orientations. It does not claim a general arbitrary-orientation classification or broad downstream applications.
